description: Figure 4.1 presents five line plots illustrating the Word Error Rate (WER) during the fine-tuning of Whisper models, each corresponding to a different model size: “tiny,” “base,” “small,” “medium,” and “large.” All plots share the same axes: the x-axis represents the “epoch,” ranging from 0 to 6 with linearly spaced integer tick marks, and the y-axis represents “WER,” scaled linearly from 0 to a maximum value specific to each plot (ranging from 30 to 70). Each plot contains multiple lines, each representing a different weight configuration for the respective model size, as indicated by the legend. In the “tiny” model plot, the lines show WER decreasing from approximately 70 to 30 over six epochs. In the “base” model plot, WER starts above 60 and decreases to around 30. The “small” model plot shows WER starting near 35 and generally decreasing to below 27.5. The “medium” model plot shows WER starting near 30 and decreasing to around 15. Finally, the “large” model plot shows WER starting near 25 and decreasing to below 10. Each line is distinguished by color, marker shape, and line style, with the legend specifying the exact configuration (e.g., “tiny AdaLoRA_int4,” “base int8,” etc.) for each.
